info.title: AnyBio Govern API
info.description: The Govern surface of the AnyBio API. Generated from the AnyBio Govern API specification, 2026-09-26.

tags.name: Govern

post.description:
Enforce answers inline (`200`); observe accepts (`202`) and evaluates off
the request path; a channel that is `off` answers `200` with
`status = not_evaluated`. A replay of a `turn_id` returns the stored
decision. `Idempotency-Key`, when sent, must equal `turn_id`.

202.description: Accepted (observe); evaluated off the request path, poll the decision id

when sent, replays the job it opened.

consent_required_channels.description: Which channels require a `granted` consent on record, resolved: the per-channel default with this application's overrides applied. Derived and read-only: `channel_policies` names only the deviations, so this answers "which channels require it" without the caller knowing the defaults.

oneOf.description: The per-patient message cap per fixed window, if any.

frequency_cap_unreadable.description:
True when the stored cap cannot be read. The cap then holds every turn
(fail-closed), so `frequency_cap: null` alone would read as "no cap"
while the gate is holding everything.

oneOf.description: The routing hand-offs opened for this application's patients are given; `null` opens them on the organization's default queue.

project_id.description: Policy scope; `null` is the organization-level active policy.

red_flag_categories.description: The red-flag categories the inbound screen runs with.

webhook_secret_hint.description: The last four characters of the webhook signing secret.

ApplicationKeyDto.description: Key metadata. Never the hash, never the secret.

expires_at.description: Set by rotation: when this key stops authenticating.

key_hint.description: The last four characters of the secret, for telling keys apart.

application_id.description: The Govern application whose patient this hand-off is about.

automation_resumed_at.description: The hold survives resolution until a person explicitly releases it.

patient_ref_hash.description: SHA-256 of the customer's opaque patient reference; never the reference.

pauses_automation.description: Whether this item also pauses automated messaging to its subject. `automation_resumed_at == null` alone says only that a person owns the item (one per patient, whichever kind it is). Automation is paused while `automation_resumed_at == null && pauses_automation`. A red flag, an exhausted budget, a missing policy, an unknown wire outcome and the Govern route-to-human path all pause; an item that only owes a patient a reply does not.

xuser_id.description: Null for Govern hand-offs; `application_id` and `patient_ref_hash` name the subject.

ChannelPolicy.description: A per-channel binding: the policy scope, the mode, and the consent requirement for one channel. An absent field means the channel's default.

project_id.description:
The project whose active policy decides this channel; `null` means the
application's `project_id`.

requires_consent.description: Whether an outbound turn on this channel requires a `granted` consent on record; absent means the channel's default (`sms`, `voice` and `email` require it).

ConsentRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/govern/patients/consent`. The reference travels in the body,
never in a path, so it is never in a request log.

at.description: When the patient granted or revoked; default now.

Counts.description:
Counts keyed by the raw gate decision (`allow`, `rewrite`,
`block_and_review`, `policy_missing`, `unavailable`) for observe turns, and
by the binding answer (`allow`, `hold`, `block`) for enforce turns.

oneOf.description:
The per-patient message cap per fixed window; none by
default.

The routing a hand-off opened for this application's patients is given: queue label, primary and backup staff, response and
escalation seconds. Staff must be members of the organization.

red_flag_categories.description:
The red-flag categories the inbound screen runs with (`cardiac`,
`respiratory`, `neuro_stroke`, `self_harm`). Default: all four.

webhook_secret.description: The webhook signing secret, shown here once.

DecisionView.description:
The decision as the contract presents it, from `evaluate` and from the
poll. `released_content` and `deliverable_content` are the only fields that
can carry message text, and each does so under a stated condition.

decision_id.description: Absent only when the channel is `off`.

deliverable_content.description:
Clinician audience only: the gate's term substitution, when there is
one to deliver. Never present for a patient audience.

oneOf.description: The hand-off this decision opened or joined, with its current state.

inbound_flags.description: The red-flag rules the inbound matched; rule ids and categories only.

model.description: The model the caller named for this turn, and its version. Null when the caller named none; never inferred.

oneOf.description: What the customer reported delivering, once it has.

released_content.description: Present once a reviewer released the held content: what to deliver.

review_url.description:
Console deep link for the customer's own reviewers, present when the
decision is in (or has been through) the review queue.

route_to_human.description:
A person must contact this patient. Independent of
`decision`: a clean draft can be `allow` with `route_to_human: true`,
and a violating one `hold` with it.

send_holding_line.description:
Send your holding line to this patient now.

This turn was stopped and the patient is waiting on a reply that is not coming, so the application sends the fixed text its clinical owner wrote: a person will reply, when, and what to do if it is urgent. **The contract says when, never what**: the text is the application's own, it is never model-written, and this service does not send it on the application's behalf.

`false` whenever another send would be the wrong thing rather than merely unnecessary: an opt-out, a missing or revoked consent, and a frequency cap each stop the turn because this patient should not be messaged, and a holding line is a message. It is also `false` in observe, where nothing was stopped and the caller was told to deliver.

One per stopped turn: each `evaluate` is one turn, so a second stopped draft in the same conversation is a second turn with its own answer.

stop_class.description:
Which of the two stopped classes this turn is: `never_sendable` | `uncertain`, null when nothing was stopped.

In **enforce** it describes the `hold` the caller received: a never-sendable turn has no release path, so the application's own reviewers are told to record a replacement rather than wait for one. In **observe** it is read beside `would_have` and describes what the stop would have been: `would_have` keeps its documented vocabulary (the raw gate decision), and this carries the class the same turn was classified with.

webhook_deliveries.description:
The signed webhook deliveries about this decision: the
log, never the body.

would_have.description:
Observe: the raw gate decision (`allow` | `rewrite` | `block_and_review`
| `policy_missing`) or `unavailable`. Null in enforce.

would_have_routed.description: Observe: the screen matched and would have routed; no task was opened.

established.description: The caller's own assertion; informational. The gate reads the ref.

ref.description:
The reference returned when THIS conversation's disclosure was
recorded. Any other value is ignored, and the turn is answered on
this conversation's own evidence, so a reference borrowed from
another conversation or application leaves the disclosure owed.

evidence_id.description: The evidence row; the id a reviewer sees in the console.

ref.description:
Attach this as `disclosure.ref` on every evaluate for the conversation.
`evaluate` also derives it from `conversation_id` when absent.

application_id.description: Optional; when present it must be the application the key is bound to.

content.description: The draft the customer's AI produced.

oneOf.description:
The patient's message this turn answers. Screened by the
deterministic red-flag floor with the application's categories; a
match routes the patient to a person. Requires `patient_ref`.

metadata.description: Free JSON, stored and never evaluated.

oneOf.description:
Advisory. The application's configured mode decides; a hint that
disagrees is ignored.

model.description:
The model the caller's application ran for this turn, as the caller
names it. Recorded, never interpreted: the platform does
not run this model and has nothing to check the name against.

model_version.description:
That model's version, as the caller names it. Independent of `model`:
a caller that versions one and not the other is recorded as it is
rather than refused.

patient_ref.description: The customer's opaque patient identifier. Stored only as a SHA-256.

turn_id.description:
The idempotency key per application: a replay returns the stored
decision. Must not start with `govern:`, which is reserved for the
rows the platform writes.

ExternalDecisionEvidence.description:
One Govern decision that opened or joined an external hand-off: the
evidence a person works from. `inbound_content` is the patient's own
message, PHI-visible on this staff-authorised surface only.

ExternalSubject.description: The subject of an external hand-off, for its readers.

patient_ref_hash.description: SHA-256 of the customer's opaque patient reference.

FrequencyCap.description:
The application's per-patient cap: at most `max_messages` per fixed window
of `window_seconds`, counted from the first message of the window.

remaining.description: Messages left in the current window (the full cap once it has lapsed).

GovernChannel.description: The channel vocabulary of the contract.

GovernMode.description:
Per policy, per application: is the gate consulted, and is its answer
binding? `Off` is not evaluated; `Observe` is evaluated and recorded as
`would_have` while the caller is always told allow; `Enforce` returns the
decision and it binds.

awaiting_reply.description: Which of these items carry a stopped draft nobody has answered yet. A patient has one open item, so a stop joins whatever they already have (a paused automation, a flagged inbound). The item keeps the reason it was opened for, and this lists what it now also owes.

HandoffRef.description: The hand-off a decision opened or joined, as the contract shows it.

pauses_automation.description:
Whether this hand-off also pauses automated messaging to the subject. `automation_resumed_at == null` says a person owns it;
this says whether the application should stop sending meanwhile. The
two are read together: still paused is
`automation_resumed_at == null && pauses_automation`.

InboundFlag.description:
One red-flag rule the inbound matched. Rule id and category only; never
the text.

InboundMessage.description: The patient's message this turn answers.

secret.description: The raw key. This is its only appearance; store it server-side.

MintedKeyDto.description: A key at mint time: the metadata plus the secret, which is shown once.

MintedWebhookSecret.description: A freshly minted signing secret: the plaintext, shown once, and when.

webhook_secret.description: The secret. This is its only appearance; store it server-side.

webhook_secret_hint.description: Its last four characters, for telling secrets apart.

ModelBreakdown.description: The same counts, per model and version the caller named. A bucket with both fields null counts the turns whose caller named no model. Send a stable model name so the report stays readable.

OptOutRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/govern/patients/opt-out`. `opted_out: false` records the
patient opting back in, which the application may do only for an opt-out
it recorded itself.

delivered.description: The customer delivered a message for this turn.

delivered_content_hash.description: SHA-256, hex, of the UTF-8 text delivered. Required when `delivered`.

delivery_ref.description: The customer's own reference for the delivery.

hash_matches_release.description:
Whether the delivered hash matches the content the record says was
deliverable. `null` when nothing was delivered or there was nothing to
compare against.

PatchApplicationRequest.description:
Every field optional; only the ones present change. `channel_policies`
replaces the whole map when present (send the full map back).

oneOf.description:
`null` clears the routing; hand-offs then open with the
organization's default queue and no deadlines.

project_id.description: `null` clears the project scope back to the organization policy.

red_flag_categories.description: Replaces the whole list when present; must not be empty.

PatientStateRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/govern/patients/state`: a read, as a POST so the reference
stays out of the URL.

PatientStateView.description: The state as the contract shows it. The reference itself is never in it.

events.description: The most recent transitions, newest first (at most twenty).

Rates.description:
Fractions in `[0, 1]`, never percentages: the share of decided observe
turns the gate would have withheld, and of decided enforce turns it held.

application_id.description: Optional; when present it must be the application the key is bound to.

text_shown.description: The disclosure text the patient was shown, verbatim.

overlap_seconds.description:
How long the previous keys keep authenticating after this rotation.
Default one day; at most seven. Zero refuses the previous keys at once.

previous_keys_expire_at.description: When every previous key of the application stops authenticating.

escalation_seconds.description: Additional elapsed time after the response deadline before backup routing.

decisions.description: Every decision record in the window, any mode or status.

transcript.description:
Records that came from a transcript batch rather than a
live call; always observe, counted in `observe` as well.

application_id.description: Optional; when present it must be the application the key is bound to.

turns.description: One to 1,000 turns; `turn_id` unique within the batch.

TranscriptJobView.description: A job as the contract presents it. Counts, never text.

abandoned.description:
Turns a failed job gave up on: never evaluated, no decision, their
text cleared with the job. Only ever non-zero when `status` is
`failed`.

unavailable.description: Evaluated turns the gate did not answer for.

would_have.description:
Raw gate decisions over the evaluated turns that are decided:
`allow`, `rewrite`, `block_and_review`, `policy_missing`,
`unavailable`.

TranscriptTurn.description: One past turn as the customer posts it.

model.description: The model that produced the turn, and its version, as the caller names them. Optional; recorded on the decision, never interpreted. Batches from before and after a model change are told apart by these.

sent_at.description: When it went out. The observe report windows on it.

turn_id.description:
The idempotency key per application: a turn the application already
has a decision for is a `duplicate`. Must not start with `govern:`,
which is reserved for the rows the platform writes.

TranscriptTurnView.description: One turn of a job, with the decision it produced or matched.

oneOf.description: Absent until the turn is processed.

WebhookDeliveryView.description:
A delivery as the contract shows it on the decision. Counts and codes,
never the body.

subject_version.description:
The revision of the subject this delivery is about: the hand-off's
`version` at the change, or `0` for an event keyed to the subject's
whole lifetime. Two deliveries of one event differ here.
